digest.component_or_area: rebar doctor (formerly link-audit) — blocking edge audit and repair
propositions: Blocking LINK events written before comparability became structural remain durable and unresolved on read, causing epic-to-child and cousin edges to distort ready/next-batch scheduling cascade.

The store-wide scan must classify each blocking edge against the CURRENT resolver rule to detect three categories: ancestor-blocking (endpoint is ancestor of other), mis-escalated (resolver returns different pair), unreadable (endpoint cannot be reduced).
Repair must write the replacement link BEFORE removing the stale one to ensure an interruption leaves a superset that the next run converges rather than losing a dependency.
Repair refuses pairs whose pair-scoped UNLINK would cancel a different relation (ambiguous-pair) because the event model offers no relation-scoped unlink.
The repair driver must not hold the store write lock across multiple writes because the non-re-entrant lock blocks its own inner acquisitions, causing 60-second timeouts and zero progress.
A read-only rebar doctor run with init_only=True must not trigger store reconvergence, and --repair must refuse to run while a reconciler pass is in flight.
